tasks.completion_summary: Fixed the HIGH break-wall dead-end found by completeness-critic review of iter39. Root cause: ExplorationHUD rendered the Break button from gameState.detectedSecrets (detected-AND-NOT-discovered, the '?' set), but ExplorationService.BreakWall requires IsDiscovered — and detected/discovered are disjoint in JournalState, so the Break button only ever showed for walls the engine rejects and vanished the moment a wall became breakable. Fix: ExplorationPresenter now emits a separate BreakableWalls list (IsDiscovered && Type=='breakable_wall' && border at (x,y,wall) still BreakableWall or CrackedWall — i.e. intact, not None/broken), each {id,x,y,wall}; added to StatePresenter payload as breakableWalls and to client GameState type as breakableWalls: BreakableWall[]. detectedSecrets kept exactly as-is (drives the '?' search affordance). ExplorationHUD: Break button(s) now render from breakableWalls (no Manhattan re-filter — BreakWall has no server distance check and discovery already required Chebyshev<=1), emit breakWall{targetId: wall.id} via typed onIntent; added data-testid='break-wall-btn'/data-secret-id; Search button unchanged. TDD (boundary tests written first, RED against current code): engine ExplorationPresenterBreakableWallTests asserts a discovered intact wall surfaces in BreakableWalls, drops out once broken (border None), and a detected-but-undiscovered wall stays out of BreakableWalls while still appearing in DetectedSecrets; client e2e break-wall.spec.ts injects presenter-shaped state, asserts a Break button renders for the discovered wall and clicking emits break_wall{targetId:'crack'} over the websocket, and asserts a detected-but-undiscovered secret gets NO Break button (only the Search affordance). Leak-hunt on the reused local RPC.Host. TWO root-cause signals. (1) Connection/session path is CLEAN: ClientRegistry.Remove runs in WebSocketConnectionHandler's finally and the per-client heartbeat loop exits on socket close; new stress test SessionLeakStressTests opens+aborts 200 WebSocket sessions and asserts the new server-side GameServer.ClientCount returns to baseline 0 -> no unbounded connection/session leak. (2) GENUINE per-frame growth leak FOUND+FIXED: StatePresenter.CreateStateMessage serialized the ENTIRE GameState.ActionLog into every state snapshot. ActionLog grows for a campaign's life (only cleared on reset_game) and the host is reused across many e2e runs locally, so each 'ready'/state-change frame's serialization cost grew O(accumulated-commands) and was fan-broadcast to all clients -- matching the reported 'per-test time balloons after many runs' symptom (code even had a dormant 1000-entry log-rotation warning, evidencing known unbounded growth). FIX: cap the snapshot's serialized actionLog to the most recent 200 entries (StatePresenter.SnapshotActionLogLimit) via a recent-tail Skip; stored ActionLog untouched so engine logic/tests are unaffected, and the client only consumes entries newer than its last-seen turn so a recent tail suffices. The 'host degrades after hours' note from iter20 is a separate compounding WSL2 GC/RSS factor; addressed deterministically by a host-restart harness: src/client/scripts/e2e-fresh.sh kills any stale RPC.Host (by :19421 and process name) before invoking Playwright on a fresh backend, wired as npm scripts test:e2e and test:e2e:fresh.
